title: channel-wire transport contract
description: See the _readme in wire.json. Byte counts are decimal integers; timings are integer milliseconds; close reasons are snake_case tokens the browser branches on. Derived values (plaintext per chunk, reassembled ceiling, hard ceiling) are NOT stored here -- the generator computes them and checks the arithmetic.

noiseAeadTagSizeBytes.description: Noise transport AEAD auth-tag overhead appended to every ciphertext. Broken out from maxCiphertextForChunk so a transport change (e.g. a post-quantum AEAD with a different tag size) is one edit instead of a tag-and-cap pair each receiver re-derives.

maxCiphertextForChunkBytes.description: Maximum ciphertext per Noise transport message. The Noise spec caps a transport message at 65535 bytes of ciphertext (a 2-byte length prefix's range); paired with noiseAeadTagSizeBytes it derives maxPlaintextPerChunkBytes.

maxMessageSizeBytes.description: Default operator-facing message size: the largest application payload a sender may hand the channel layer. Operators may raise or lower it via max_message_size; the effective per-channel value is min(hub, worker), announced at open. Producers that clamp input bound by THIS, not the reassembled ceiling: what the receiver caps is the payload plus every envelope around it. When the payload budget equalled the reassembled ceiling, a producer that filled its budget exactly built an inner message the receiver refused mid-stream -- and the ordered, encrypted stream has no resync path.

innerEnvelopeHeadroomBytes.description: What maxReassembledMessageSizeBytes adds on top of a payload budget, covering the envelopes a payload is wrapped in before the wire -- the widest fan-out is AgentChatMessage -> AgentEvent -> WatchEventsResponse -> InnerStreamMessage -> InnerMessage. Real overhead is field tags, varint lengths and ids: kilobytes, not hundreds; the slack is deliberate so adding a field to any envelope cannot quietly reintroduce a mid-stream drop.

maxConfigurableMessageSizeBytes.description: Largest max_message_size an operator may configure. Caps worst-case per-channel reassembly memory (maxIncompleteChunked * maxReassembledMessageSizeBytes).

pingMethod.description: The no-op inner RPC a client issues once, before OpenChannel returns, to prove the E2EE session works end to end. Noise_NK's handshake only proves the client can encrypt to the worker's static key; without a round trip at open time a session broken in either direction opens 'successfully' and fails later on the first real call -- and pooled channels cache that broken session. It carries no payload: the proof is that the round trip decrypts at both ends.

protocolVersion.description: The ChannelMessage envelope version every sender stamps (NewChannelMessage, the bypassing Go senders, and the browser's channelSession).

tooManyConnections.description: Sent when a user already holds as many long-lived connections as max_connections_per_user allows. A client branches on it: every other policy-violation close means 're-authenticate', this one means 'close a tab' -- opposite advice.

snapshotTooLarge.description: Sent when a /ws/userevents subscriber's opening snapshot exceeds the whole queue budget. A frame bigger than the pool's capacity is refused at EVERY occupancy, so retry-later advice would loop forever rebuilding the same oversized snapshot; only an operator can fix it (raise userevents_queue_memory_budget), so the close is final and says so.

forbidden.description: Sent when the authenticated user may not have what they asked for -- an ACL check that said no, not a credential that expired. Re-authenticating does not grant a permission and reloading asks again, so neither advice helps.

controlFlood.description: Sent when a peer keeps sending control frames past what its allowance absorbs. A misbehaving or misconfigured client, not a user error: nothing about the account, workspace, or credential is wrong. Clears on reload because the new socket starts with a full allowance.

hardNonceLimit.description: The uint32 wrap bound: the last nonce value the counter may hold before a rekey is mandatory. 2^32-1; the generator checks hardNonceLimit > softNonceLimit.

lengthPrefixBytes.description: Pinned to 4: both framers (Go WriteFramedBytes/ReadFramedBytes, TS frameBytes/unframeBytes) write a big-endian uint32. The constant documents the width; it does not parameterize it.
